title: Monetary Policy and Targeted Measures to Rein in Food and Accommodation Prices
what_it_is: Monetary Policy and Targeted Measures to Rein in Food and Accommodation Prices

sections.label: MAS monetary policy tightening
sections.summary: MAS tightened monetary policy a fifth time in 13 months by re-centring the S$NEER policy band mid-point, expecting firm core inflation into first half 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In October, it tightened monetary policy for a fifth time in the last 13 months, by re-centring up the mid-point of the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate (S$NEER) policy band.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: MAS expects core inflation to stay firm for the rest of this year and into the first half of 2023, before slowing more discernibly in the second half.

sections.label: Effects of tightening moves
sections.summary: The five monetary policy tightening moves are estimated to dampen core inflation by an average of 1.5 percentage points yearly over 2022 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The cumulative effects of the five monetary policy tightening moves are estimated to dampen core inflation by an average of 1.5 percentage points each year, over 2022 to 2023.

sections.label: MAS exchange rate target
sections.summary: MAS uses the nominal exchange rate, not interest rates, as the intermediate target of monetary policy, unlike most central banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Yesterday, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim said in this House, and I quote, "I am befuddled because even now, the Government routinely alters levers or policies, such as the interest rate where there is uncertainty on a year-to-year basis about the level of interest rate".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I wanted to clarify that, unlike most central banks which target interest rates, MAS uses the nominal exchange rate as the intermediate target of monetary policy.

sections.label: MAS reserves accumulation
sections.summary: MAS accumulated more than $200 billion of reserves in 2021, higher and faster than the normal $40 billion to $50 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because we have been accumulating reserves at a much higher, faster rate, than in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We all know, by now, that in 2021, MAS had accumulated more than $200 billion of reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our normal rate of accumulation is about $40 billion to $50 billion a year.

sections.label: Exchange rate to manage inflation
sections.summary: MAS uses the exchange rate, not interest rate, to manage inflation, and has been careful and calibrated in monetary policy given a fluid global environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: MAS, because of our open trade architecture, we use our exchange rate, not our interest rate, to manage inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The global environment, as the hon Member knows, is very fluid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That is why, over the course of a year, we have been very careful, very calibrated in our approach towards monetary policy.
